notes: Case file notes: which story choices appear in the case file, as established or still open. Every text is copied verbatim from that choice's approved response; ContentValidator-style checks in CaseFileCatalog enforce it.

entries.text: You retain responsibility for the outstanding clinical review and follow-up. No clinical task is marked completed. The records discrepancy can be investigated separately.
Comparison recorded as unresolved. Request the authorized source-system export and preservation of the originals before drawing conclusions.
Request submitted for authorized Records review. Source access and reconciliation remain pending. The originals must be retained; no independent corroboration or loss of time is established.
Clock review recorded: no correction can be justified yet. Raw offsets, clock authority and synchronization history remain requested. The displayed mismatch remains unresolved.
Export-order review recorded. Preserve the original representation and request its sort key, raw event sequence and transformation history. Do not reorder or overwrite the original.
Dependency review recorded: source independence remains unestablished. Request original capture, clock authority, extraction history and shared dependencies before counting corroboration.

Preservation follow-up recorded. Request confirmation of original receipt, unchanged source bytes/checksum and custody history from authorized Records staff. Receipt and preservation remain unconfirmed.

Unresolved memo recorded with clock-authority/offset verification prioritized. Records must also address ordering, lineage, custody and preservation. Source receipt and any reconciliation remain pending. Return to Naomi to acknowledge the outstanding work.

Unresolved memo recorded with source-lineage/custody verification prioritized. Records must also address clock authority, offsets, ordering and preservation. Source receipt and any reconciliation remain pending. Return to Naomi to acknowledge the outstanding work.
Factual scope recorded. Talk to Voss again about what the follow-up still needs.

Missing permissions recorded:
Information Security: audit of the inactive credential and who could use it.
Records: the pending preservation and source-export request, with clock and ordering metadata.
Security: any question about W0-B access policy. No inspection is authorized.
Clinical follow-up stays with you and the nursing team.
Follow-up recorded: written process requested. The records discrepancy and the credential audit remain unresolved.
Follow-up recorded: independent reconciliation proposed. The source request, preservation confirmation and credential audit remain pending.

Referral sent to the authorized Records office: two copies, two dates, origin of each copy to be checked. No finding about the records is made, and nothing in Mara's clinical assessment changes. Her follow-up (sleep and function support, safety follow-up, legal-role clarification, medication reconciliation) stays with the clinical team.
Candidates logged: clock skew, migrated location codes, export sorting, identifier collision. Each may explain part of the discrepancy; none is confirmed. The discrepancy stays unresolved.
Next check recorded: source extraction requested through Records' authorized process. It tests clock skew and export sorting once received. Nothing is received yet; every candidate stays open.
Next check recorded: identifier crosswalk between legacy and current codes. It tests migrated location codes and identifier collision. Clock and ordering questions stay open.
Next check recorded: neutral second review requested. A reviewer outside the team re-checks the candidates and the method. No candidate is confirmed in the meantime.
Question recorded. Ask Hale for one permitted follow-up.
Follow-up recorded: clinical risk check requested. No patient is moved and no access changes.
Follow-up recorded: permitted report summary requested. The credential audit stays with Information Security.
Follow-up recorded: archived facilities plans requested. No route or access is authorized.

Recorded as reported: heard what sounded like the old lift bell during a scheduled shutdown; possibly the test cycle; did not see anyone use the lift. This is witness memory, not an observation of movement.
Follow-up recorded: confirm scheduled work orders. The bell may match a test; nothing is concluded yet.
Follow-up recorded: the statement stands in the technician's own words, including "could've been the test cycle" and "I wouldn't say I did". No inference is added.
Follow-up recorded: timing to be checked against shift and work-order records. No time is assigned from memory.
Scope recorded: lobby doors only, with an escort. Lift, service hatch and W0-B remain locked.
Documented: doors closed and latched at first check; ajar on return; the escort and you did not watch them continuously in between. No cause is recorded.
The doors are pushed shut and the latch engages. Security has the report: found ajar during an escorted check, cause unknown.
Request recorded: Facilities to check the lobby door latch and the corridor ventilation pressure. The doors were found ajar after an unwatched interval; no cause is assumed.
Recorded in the incident record: two export representations disagree on the access-event date; time-zone provenance unreconciled. Mara's clinical note is unchanged and kept separate.
Escalation requested through the audit process. Both versions stay as received; no date is chosen.
Both versions are preserved separately with their provenance. Neither is treated as corroborating the other.
Independent technical review requested. Until it reports, the date stays unresolved.

Report recorded: part of the timing mismatch is explained by clock differences; the remainder of the reported interval cannot be reconstructed from the available records. Source, preservation and audit requests remain open.
Clinical coverage confirmed.

The summary lists what Chapter 2 left open: an inactive credential in the transfer-request audit, export versions that disagree on a date, an unwatched door found ajar and a witness who heard but did not see. Nothing in it is resolved.
Scope recorded: you attend for the transfer-workflow question only. The building survey belongs to Security and Facilities.
Logged: current and historic level datums differ; no conclusion drawn.
The historic plan shows this threshold and a corridor beyond; the current map shows nothing below the sealed corridor. Logged as a plan-edition difference.
Stencils read LOWER LEVEL B and SERVICE B. The plate's wording matches the archival plan's room schedule. No sign uses the W0-B code itself; the designation remains the plan's.
Documented with the time: inner door closed, frame intact, dust undisturbed except along the team's marked line, one radiator, one lamp working.
Hale walks it with you: threshold, opened infill, sealed corridor, mechanical corridor, stair. One route, physically continuous, marked.
Two later editions agree with what is built; the oldest puts it one bay earlier. Annotated with the reference points. Cause unknown.
Engineer: I'll add it to the survey request with measured reference points. Until then it's a drawing discrepancy.
Logged as found: built position and one plan edition differ by one bay. Renovation and drawing error both remain possible.
The team holds at the authorized point. Inspection paused for a route check.
One approved, physically continuous route back.
Debrief recorded: similar landmarks, an uncertain plan revision, one unreconciled location note, two plan areas with the same label. Each statement under its own name.
Survey request supported; repeat entry remains suspended.
Marked unresolved_measurement: values, instruments, reference points and times kept as taken.
Protocol requested: same reference points, calibrated instruments, logged clocks, two independent teams.
Restricted status maintained. No entry until the protocol and safety authorization are in place.
Report submitted. Access remains restricted.
Voss: Good. Both files say what was observed and what wasn't.

Official finding entered: plan editions and observations disagree; cause unresolved; independent review pending. The first draft is kept in the revision history.
Rahman: Both are important. Different questions need different evidence.
Both originals preserved. Checks listed: display-difference correction, clock-source comparison, custody trail. Independence documented per record. The time-order contradiction stands.
Recorded: controlled watch with no door movement; an authorized entry between the original checks is not excluded; logs and inspection results preserved. Repeatability open.
Voss: Agreed. An outside team with its own instruments, under Hale's restriction.
Voss: One briefing, three obligations: care, safety, record. I'll schedule it.
Voss: Noted in the record under your name. The restriction and the care plan stand.
Logged twice, independently written: panel 17, diagonal crack, beside the alcove. Time noted on both sheets.
Voss: Filed. Observed repetition, unverified. Both sheets attached as written.
Hale: Logged. New sheets, new notes, originals untouched.
Rahman: I'm covering the ward. Nobody upstairs goes without.
Both recordings logged as they are, with their clock sources. The contradiction is preserved as an unresolved observation.
Timeline rebuilt from authenticated entries. Unauthenticated entries listed separately.
Unknown-provenance entries flagged, not removed.
Archival gaps and proven misconduct filed under separate headings. Nothing moved between them without evidence.
Analyst: That's what the evidence supports.
Analyst: Agreed. Bounded, documented, stoppable.
Questions answered within your role; the follow-up handed to the receiving team with a named deadline before evening handoff.
Rahman: Then let's make sure that's how it's reported.
Voss: Then we prepare a factual referral.
Hale: That's a defensible safety position.
Rahman: As long as patient care and access controls are protected.
You: Frustration doesn't make your questions irrelevant.
